summary: Full backend + frontend E2E validation of LABOS Technologies after requirements.txt --extra-index-url change. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (31 pytest cases across services, auth, bookings, payments, admin, contact) — 31/31 passing. Frontend: Playwright validated home, services, register, login (client + admin), booking (package + quote), Stripe checkout redirect (both from /book and from dashboard Pay button), admin dashboard stats/tabs/edit-modal with persistence, client visibility of quoted amount + admin note, contact form success toast, mobile nav, protected-route enforcement (client hitting /admin is redirected to /dashboard). Only 2 minor issues found; no critical defects.

minor.issue: No brute-force protection: 7 consecutive invalid password attempts all returned 401 (no lockout/429/backoff). Playbook expects lockout after 5 failed attempts.
Services catalog is static in code (services_catalog.py); no admin CRUD — acceptable by design, noted only for future.

ui_bugs.issue: No catch-all 404 route — navigating to an unknown path (e.g. /does-not-exist) renders a completely blank page (empty body, no navbar/footer).

integration_issues.issue: Clicking Book Package on /services when not logged in redirects to /login but the intended destination (?service=&package=) is not preserved; after login the user lands on /dashboard and must re-pick the package. Minor UX regression, not a functional break.

issues: Data loads without skeleton — bare 'Loading...' text flashes before content; empty-state test id only appears after fetch resolves (cosmetic).

action_items: Add a catch-all <Route path="*"> 404 page in App.js — unknown URLs currently render a blank white/black page.
Add login brute-force lockout (e.g. 5 failed attempts -> temporary 429) as required by the auth playbook.
Optional: preserve the intended /book?service=...&package=... redirect target through the login flow.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py CORS fallback `or ["*"]` combined with allow_credentials=True would be rejected by browsers if CORS_ORIGINS were ever empty; currently .env sets explicit origins so it is fine, but the wildcard fallback should be removed.

GET /api/payments/status/{session_id} has no auth/ownership check — any caller who knows a session_id can read its payment status and trigger a Stripe poll. Consider requiring the authenticated owner.
@app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') is deprecated in current FastAPI; migrate to lifespan handlers.
PATCH /api/admin/bookings strips falsy values via `if v is not None` on exclude_unset dump — OK, but amount=0 is accepted and would create a $0 payable booking; add amount > 0 validation.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all core flows pass; 404 route + login redirect-target are the misses)

seed_data_creation: Registered client test_fe_1787584569@labos.dev / Test@1234 (has one $499 package booking pending and one quote booking quoted at $2,500 with admin note). Several test_client_*/test_reg_*@labos.dev users, TEST_-prefixed bookings and 'TEST subject ...' contacts created by pytest.
test_credentials: Admin admin@labos.tech / Labos@2026 works and returns role=admin. Client test_fe_1787584569@labos.dev / Test@1234. /app/memory/test_credentials.md accurate (client@test.com is not pre-registered — register-on-demand as documented).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py — use `service_slug` (NOT service_id) in POST /api/bookings. pytest.ini uses -n 2 --dist loadscope, so do NOT share state via class attributes across test classes; use session-scoped fixtures (package_booking/quote_booking) as done here. Stripe sk_test_emergent works end-to-end up to the hosted checkout page ($499 and $2,500 sessions verified); payment completion was intentionally not performed so payment_status stays 'pending' and admin revenue stat is $0.
rca_of_the_issue: Blank unknown-route page: App.js <Routes> defines only explicit paths with no path="*" fallback, so React Router matches nothing and renders an empty tree. Brute-force gap: /api/auth/login has no failed-attempt counter or rate limiter in server.py.
